sample.title: Why India Won’t Break Up With Russia
sample.description:
India has spent decades balancing its ties to Russia, and the USSR before it, with those to the US. Today, Russia remains a major supplier of oil and weapons to India, just as India builds deeper economic and strategic ties with the US. 

And while India and Russia have changed over time, their relationship remains strong. Even amid the Kremlin’s war on Ukraine and intense pressure from Washington, New Delhi won’t let Moscow go. So why does India keep Russia so close, and can it keep up this balancing act?

sample.description:

Bracket22 invests only Kelly's own capital and trades cryptocurrencies, stocks and commodities. It's powered entirely by AI agents — a stark example of a growing reality on Wall Street as firms test the benefits and limits of AI in finance.

sample.title: Why Election Officials Are Worried About Prediction Markets
sample.description:
Delaware County, Pennsylvania, and Maricopa County, Arizona, have adopted policies addressing employee prediction market activity. Officials say the rules are meant to prevent financial conflicts, protect workers from allegations and reassure voters, not respond to evidence that election workers have used the markets. sample.title: Houthis claim major advance on Red Sea coast | BBC News
sample.description:
Tit-for-tat strikes have continued in Yemen between the Iranian-backed Houthi rebels and pro-government forces aligned to Saudi Arabia. 
 
It comes after a series of military advances by the Houthis, which threaten Saudi oil production. 
 
Those significant territorial gains along the western coast in recent days, including taking Perim Island, a key strategic point next to the Bab al-Mandab Strait, could give the Houthis a possible stronger hold over the strategic waterway.

MPs and Lords call for new law to address AI threat to human rights | BBC News
sample.description:
A cross-party group of MPs and peers has identified human rights risks posed by artificial intelligence (AI) which existing laws, they argue, are ill-equipped to cover.
 
The Joint Committee on Human Rights published a report calling for a new bill on AI to "address the scale and seriousness" of such threats.
 
"Nowhere in the world, including the UK, has a current legislative and regulatory approach to AI that is fit for purpose," said Labour MP and committee chair Alex Sobel.

sample.title: Linkin Park’s Joe Hahn: Why acknowledging the criticism was essential | BBC News
sample.description:
After Chester Bennington's death in 2017, Linkin Park went on an indefinite hiatus. In 2024, the band returned with new music and a new co-vocalist, Emily Armstrong.
 
But what happened behind closed doors during the years in between? In their new documentary film Unshatter, Linkin Park share the process of deciding to make music together again.
 
BBC News' Mel Ramsay speaks with band member and Unshatter director Joe Hahn about navigating grief as well as dealing with criticism - and why the band felt ready to return.
